anomalies.observed: On sheet /, D2 is drawn with a diode symbol (triangle + cathode bar) and the reference prefix D2, but its value field reads '1K'. It is connected between NET0006 and GND, while R6 (10K) pulls NET0006 up to +5V. NET0006 is also the MCU pin PB4 (U1.3 / U2.2).
anomalies.expected: A two-terminal part's reference prefix, symbol and value must agree: a diode should carry a part number / voltage rating, not a resistance, and a '1K' value implies a resistor (R-prefix, rectangular symbol). As drawn, a diode to GND on a 10K-pulled-up signal net clamps that net to ~0.7 V, so PB4 cannot carry a valid high/tach signal.

evidence.quote: D2 symbol = diode, value = '1K', between NET0006 and GND (sheet /, row B/C)
R6 10K between +5V and NET0006; U1 pin 3 = XTAL2/PB4 = NET0006, U2 pin 2 = PB4 = NET0006
the specification is silent on the fan controller's internals ('an ATtiny-driven fan controller'), so the part must be judged against standard practice and its own metadata

anomalies.impact: PB4 (NET0006) is held at a fixed low voltage by the diode clamp (or, if a 1K resistor was intended, mis-biased by the 10K/1K divider), so any function on PB4 (e.g. tachometer input or a status line) reads a constant value; the diode-with-resistance-value mismatch also indicates an assembly/sourcing or editing error.
